tasks.derivation: The plot is approximately linear and negative. The line predicts 0.7 fewer minutes of exercise per day per extra minute of daily television, with predicted 64.3 minutes at zero television. At x=42 the prediction is 34.9 minutes; at x=120 it is −19.7 minutes, impossible, and 120 is outside the displayed data range.
tasks.sourceFidelity: All four parts and shared equation retained; stated mark allocations omitted. Embedded SVG image bytes equal the original PNG. The plot remains raster, with no editable individual points.

requiredEdits.target: part b short and worked answers
requiredEdits.issue: The slope wording states that exercise decreases as viewing increases without identifying the regression prediction, implying a causal or deterministic individual change.
requiredEdits.repair: State that each additional minute per day of television is associated with a decrease of 0.7 minutes per day in predicted average exercise, according to this regression line.

tasks.difficultyReason: Interpret the supplied coefficients in context and combine substitution with a judgment about extrapolation; the model and graph are supplied.

tasks.derivation: The plotted points follow a decreasing curve that flattens, so the relationship is nonlinear. Reading between (5,92) and (9,87) at y=90 gives roughly 6–7 m; about 6 m is reasonable.
tasks.sourceFidelity: Both parts and mark omission preserved; native grid, broken vertical axis, labels and eight plotted points match the original image.
tasks.difficultyReason: Identify the visible curved pattern and estimate an x-value directly from the plotted trend.

tasks.derivation: Independent least-squares calculation gives slope −53.3869602, intercept 748.9784081 and Pearson r=−0.9211732195; rounding gives P=748.98−53.39R and r=−0.92, a strong negative correlation. At R=10, the rounded line gives 215.08 thousand and the unrounded fit 215.109 thousand, both $215,000 to the nearest thousand.
tasks.sourceFidelity: Nine data pairs and all four prompts and answers retained, with source marks omitted.
tasks.difficultyReason: Use technology on a two-variable table, interpret the sign and strength of correlation, then predict and convert thousands to dollars.

tasks.derivation: The 30 original inline points include exactly (18,24) and (25,24) with both coordinates under 30. The supplied line goes from (0,13.2) to (100,58.2), giving gradient 0.45 and S=13.2+0.45M. The association is positive, with substantial scatter; high-M examples such as (95,35) refute the universal claim. Computing directly from the supplied points as a check gives r≈0.575 before and 0.677 after removing (25,55), confirming that it increases toward 1. The source calls the correlation weak; strength labels are convention dependent.
tasks.sourceFidelity: All 30 source inline coordinates and trendline are identical in the native TikZ, all six parts are intact and marks omitted. Approximate readings in the worked gradient are consistent with the drawn line.
tasks.difficultyReason: Read a scatterplot and line, refute a universal claim with counterexamples, and reason how removing an outlier affects positive correlation without calculation.

representativeAssessment.reason: The four complete tasks contribute contextual coefficient interpretation, nonlinear form and graph reading, table-based calculation of regression and r, and a concrete outlier-removal effect. These add to the supplied current 12 comparison coverage; this is not a broad source census.
